name: agent-dispatch-supervisor-self-update
description: Tier-P F1 scenario: install + provision agent-dispatch on a fresh box, then drive the `supervise serve` singleton daemon's own live version-staleness check (#2259) through a battery of real process-level checks -- (default-on-handoff) with NO env var set, a stale `current-version` marker triggers a real self-triggered handoff: the daemon winds down, releases its single-instance lease, spawns a successor on the newer interpreter, and exits with the distinct self-update code, and the singleton lease ends up held by a genuinely different, live successor process; (opt-out-disables) the same stale marker with the opt-out env var set keeps the ORIGINAL daemon alive with no handoff; (no-marker-fail-safe) with no `current-version` marker at all the daemon also stays alive (fail-safe default). Proves the check is armed WITHOUT any opt-in step -- this harness has no launch-path protocol to flip an opt-in flag before a daemon's first boot, so default-on is the only shape that actually activates for real operators. The heavy orchestration lives in a portable stdlib-only probe so it is verifiable off-Docker too. Name-free / public.
